parts.label: Step 2

questions.q: Name the polymer made from propene.
questions.model: Rule: put 'poly' in front of the monomer's name in brackets. Monomer: propene. So poly(propene).

questions.q: What happens to the C=C bond in polymerisation?
questions.a: It opens to a single bond, letting monomers join.

questions.q: Which is better for a rigid bottle, LDPE or HDPE?
Core: Draw (or describe) three ethene monomers joining into part of a poly(ethene) chain.
questions.a: Three C₂H₄ units; double bonds become single; carbons join in a chain with extended bonds at each end.
questions.model: Teacher draws the first monomer, then opens its double bond and links it to the next carbon.

questions.q: Extend: Compare LDPE and HDPE: structure, properties, one use each.
questions.a: LDPE: branched, low density, flexible, bags; HDPE: straight, packed, rigid, bottles.

questions.q: Stretch: Why does poly(ethene) not decolourise bromine water but ethene does?
questions.a: The polymer has no C=C double bonds left to react.

questions.q: Big question: how can one small molecule become a plastic bag?
questions.a: Thousands of ethene molecules open their double bonds and join into long poly(ethene) chains.
